meta.celebration_photo_note: Default celebration_photo above (added v1.5) is the Queen Bee screen's background photo, used by ALL themes for now — same shared-default pattern as background.light being null pending per-theme values. To give a specific theme its own celebration photo later, add a celebration_photo object (same shape: filename/credit/crop/alt) directly to that theme entry; loadTheme() should prefer a theme's own celebration_photo over this meta default when present. Mutisia and Calendula currently have no override and will keep using this default.

meta.progression_note: Clockwise: lower_left (7 o'clock) → left (9) → upper_left (11) → upper_right (1) → right (3) → lower_right (5) → center. This is the normal clockwise direction of analog clock hands.
meta.border_note: No border on any hex — dark background provides sufficient separation between lit and unlit cells
meta.text_color_note: Dark text on light hexes; white on mid-to-dark hexes
meta.start_note: honeycomb.start.center/outer give the honeycomb's pre-game colors (added v1.3): center starts at a muted version of the Genius hue so it reads as the required-letter landmark from game load; outer hexes start at a warm very-dark neutral, lighter than fully unlit.
meta.background_note: background.dark (added v1.3) is the screen background for this theme, same hue family as unlit/start.outer but darker, so honeycomb hexes remain the visual focus. background.light is scaffolded as null pending a future light-theme prompt.
meta.chrome_text_note: honeycomb.chrome_text (added v1.4) is the color for rank label + score numbers in the UI chrome (outside the honeycomb itself). Deliberately reuses an EXISTING level color rather than a separately tuned accent, so chrome text can never clash with the honeycomb — it's literally drawn from the same palette. The specific rank chosen (4 or 5) varies per theme based on which level tests best for contrast against that theme's background; see each theme's chrome_text.role for the exact reasoning and contrast ratio. Genius (rank 7) is deliberately NOT used here — it's reserved for the cta field below so the 'peak' color stays visually special rather than appearing in everyday UI text.
meta.cta_note: honeycomb.cta (added v1.4) is the Enter button's fill + label_text. Always sourced from rank 7 (Genius) — the theme's most saturated color — since Enter is the primary, most-frequently-pressed action and deserves the theme's strongest visual weight. label_text is NOT uniformly white: it's whichever of white/near-black (#1a0f00) tests better against that theme's specific Genius fill. Mutisia and Yellow Bells need near-black (their Genius colors are bright/saturated enough that white fails WCAG AA); Calendula needs white (its Genius color is dark enough that white wins). Do not assume white is always correct — check contrast per theme before reusing this pattern for new themes.
meta.dominant_emoji_note: honeycomb.dominant_emoji (added v1.6) is the single Unicode colored-square/circle emoji used for the plain-text share fallback (share-by-text feature), when the real canvas-rendered honeycomb image can't be attached. Hand-picked per theme to approximate that theme's Genius-level hue — Unicode only offers ~9 fixed colors (🔴🟠🟡🟢🔵🟣🟤⚫️⚪️), so this is a coarse approximation, not a color match. Deliberately NOT derived from a hex value at runtime — CVD-safe color choice for this fallback path is a human judgment call, not a nearest-neighbor computation. Current picks are a reasonable starting point (Mutisia and Calendula share 🟠 since both read as orange-leaning at Genius saturation) — adjust freely to taste, this field has no other consumer.
